newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Act will safeguard NZ's economic growth - Prebble.
newsitem.headline: Act will safeguard NZ's economic growth - Prebble.

text.p: Act New Zealand leader Richard Prebble said his radical free-market party would have a profound influence in the next parliament and would use it to ensure that New Zealand's economic growth was not compromised.
With 67.9 percent of the vote counted in New Zealand's first general election under the new Mixed Member Proportional (MMP) system, ACT is projected to win eight seats in the new parliament.
"I think you'll find when parliament meets, the Act MPs will have a very profound influence not only on the parliament but on the debate," Prebble told TV3.

"We are in favour of seeing our present economic growth not compromised, but we want to see the tough issues of health and education tackled and in an MMP parliament, we're going to be able to do that."

Prebble won the electorate seat of Wellington central and his party is currently polling around 6.1 percent of the party vote. Act is seen as a natural coalition partner for National, whose leader Jim Bolger declined to rule out the possibility of a minority government.
Labour, New Zealand First and the left-wing Alliance have a majority of seats and could oust National if they were able to agree terms to govern.
Prebble said Act would act as an anchor for the whole legislature.

"We will improve the standard of discussion in the New Zealand parliament, and that's got to be good for the whole country," he said. "I'm going to try and act as an anchor for the whole of the parliament."
